risk_if_not_implemented: Without Information Sharing With Third Parties, supplier and External Service Provider (ESP) weaknesses, incidents or failures may propagate into the organization's environment unmanaged. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Access (R-AC-4), Regulatory / Legal / Contractual Financial Liability (R-EX-5), Loss of Confidentiality (R-IP-2), Privacy Harm / Unauthorized Processing (R-IP-6), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Statutory / Regulatory / Contractual Change (MT-11), Data Quality Degradation / Data Poisoning (MT-12).

compensating_control_1.name: Third-Party Contract Requirements
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to require contractual requirements for applicable security, compliance and resilience requirements with third-parties, reflecting the organization's needs to protect its Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD).
compensating_control_1.justification: Third-Party Contract Requirements (TPM-14) provides third-party oversight that compensates for the absence of Information Sharing With Third Parties (PRI-16) by extending security obligations contractually and monitoring third-party risk in lieu of direct control. Given the data-handling focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Sensitive / Regulated Data Sharing Decisions
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a process to assist users in making information sharing decisions to ensure data is appropriately protected.
compensating_control_2.justification: Sensitive / Regulated Data Sharing Decisions (DCH-08.1) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Information Sharing With Third Parties (PRI-16) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Data applicability. Given the data-handling focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
